newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan to raise penalties for human smuggling.
newsitem.headline: Japan to raise penalties for human smuggling.

text.p: Faced with a surge in illegal immigrants, Japan plans to boost the maximum jail term for smuggling workers into the country from 18 months to 10 years, a Justice Ministry spokesman said on Wednesday.

In a further crackdown on the organisers of the human smuggling rings, the fines for such offences will rise to a maximum of 10 million yen ($81,300) from 150,000 yen ($1,219), the spokesman told reporters.
The proposed revisions to the Immigration Control Law will be submitted to parliament for enactment later this month.
Under the current law, the organisers of the immigration rings face lighter punishment than the illegal entrants themselves.
"We hope these stiff penalties will be a deterrent against the current rush of illegal immigrants," the spokesman said.
In the first two months of this year, a record 581 illegal Chinese immigrants were arrested by Japanese authorities, already more than last year's total of 545 people.
The brokers are known as "Snakeheads" for their reputed viciousness and the problems faced in countering them.
Many illegal immigrants came in boats from Fujian and other densely populated coastal areas of China, lured by the prospect of high wages in Japan.
In the first crackdown this year on groups suspected of organising the boat trips, Japanese police last month arrested seven suspected members of a Japan-based gang of Chinese smugglers. ($1=123 yen)
